interview.lead: Answer spines you can verify against the cited pages, then the question from each task.

spines.title: Xid 79
spines.answer: The GPU has fallen off the bus: it is no longer reachable over PCIe. NVIDIA's catalog says restart the bare-metal host and contact support, since it often points to a PCIe link or hardware failure.

spines.title: Xid 48, 63, 64
spines.answer: 48 is an uncorrectable double-bit ECC error. 63 records a row-remapping event and is informational. 64 is a row-remap failure and needs a GPU reset or escalation.

spines.title: algbw versus busbw
spines.answer: algbw is size divided by time. busbw applies a correction so the number is comparable to link bandwidth regardless of rank count: all-reduce multiplies by 2(n-1)/n.

spines.title: DCGM r3 versus r2
spines.answer: r3 adds the diagnostic, targeted stress, targeted power, NVBandwidth and NCCL plugins on top of r2's software, PCIe and NVLink, memory and memory bandwidth tests.

spines.title: GPUDirect RDMA requirements
spines.answer: GPU and NIC under the same upstream PCIe root complex for good performance; IOMMU disabled or pass-through; peer memory module loaded.

spines.title: Multi-node all-reduce bar
spines.answer: One public guide uses roughly 92% of theoretical fabric bandwidth as the pass line, for example 370 GB/s on a 400 GB/s fabric. State your own threshold and why.

spines.title: Remediation loop
spines.answer: Use a circuit breaker so a cluster-wide event cannot cordon every node. Reset one GPU when the fault is recoverable; reboot the node only when needed.

spines.title: Pass/fail semantics
spines.answer: Define thresholds in a file. A job that finishes but misses its target is still a failure.

certifications.title: NCP-AII (NVIDIA-Certified Professional: AI Infrastructure)
certifications.html:
NVIDIA's exam page (checked Oct 8, 2026): 120 minutes, 70-75 questions, $400, online with remote proctoring (Certiverse), valid for two years. Recommended background: two to three years of data-center operations with NVIDIA hardware; treat the labs here as your substitute and read the page before you book.

Domain weights as published in NVIDIA's exam study guide (reported by third-party guides; confirm in the official guide): Cluster Test and Verification 33%, Systems and Server Bring-up 31%, Control Plane Installation and Configuration 19%, Troubleshooting and Optimization 12%, Physical Layer Management 5%. Phases 1-3 of this roadmap line up with the first three domains.
